sections.value:
BLOCK: re-registration can reverse the order of activity publications.

B284-1 (normal-use correctness): .copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:2408-2414.
republishActivity queues a closure that reads activityObserved when it executes,
whereas observeActivity queues first sends with their state captured at observation.
While an earlier activity request is in flight, a heartbeat re-registration can
enqueue its re-publish ahead of working -> idle -> working transitions. The exact
head sends: idle, working (the newest state, read by the re-publish), working,
idle (the older queued transition), working. Thus an older idle overwrites a newer
working already accepted by the daemon. Serial HTTP requests alone do not prevent
this reordering; attempt zero is deliberately exempt from the supersession guard.
This violates packet points 4 and 5 and can falsely expose a working seat as idle.

Repair control: capture the registration's state when enqueuing its re-publication.
Changing only the lazy activityObserved argument to the already-captured state
makes the in-flight registration regression green. Preserve that regression with
the fix; the normal event first-send order must remain intact.

Non-blocking notes:
- store.mjs:2424-2425,2465-2471: when working and idle are observed before the first
  queued working request starts, that stale request captures idle's new retry
  controller. If it fails, idle waits through its initial 1-second retry delay.
  A stale-state check before scheduling the wait fixes this separate, bounded
  failure of the promised immediate supersession. Both small repairs pass all
  five additional probes and preserve the 15 existing selected activity/F230 tests.
- Retry wording/cost: one episode is one initial attempt plus at most five retries,
  with waits 1,2,5,10,30 seconds (48 seconds of waits, excluding HTTP time).
  There is no unbounded repeat of the 30-second slot. Exhaustion clears activityState:
  another same-state root event, or another registration, starts a fresh episode.
  A deterministic unchanged-state probe produces 6 attempts, then another 6.
  Therefore neither indefinite "until it lands" nor "5 retries per state change"
  is the correct lifetime guarantee. The existing 400/422 context fallback can add RPCs.

Batch-path proof:
The busy exemption is exactly Copilot AND native_extension_delivery. The added
scope probe covers both native flags for Copilot, OMP, Pi, Claude and Codex.
Other busy owners still accumulate, and --fyi remains held without waking.
The persisted last_wake_at floor survives service reconstruction; it is per job,
not an aggregate per-owner limit. Batch numbers are allocated at cut time, not
consumption time: events remain pending in the durable open batch until handoff
settles. Reconstructing the service after admission but before settlement retains
that batch and admits it only once; following events are neither lost nor duplicated.

Validation:
- just pr-freeze 284: FINAL when the review began at
  16b75f3b8bc510e8a305ecd7ca49044b3be27b1c; all latest CI checks passed.
  At closeout the head is unchanged and those checks still pass, but GitHub
  reports DIRTY against newer main. Reconcile that conflict and freeze the new
  head for round 2. This verdict covers only the requested head/base.
- just copilot-native-test: 366 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed.
- PIJ_SHARED_TARGET="$(bash harness/scripts/cargo-target.sh)" just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --lib background::tests -- --nocapture: 82 passed.
- Private exact-head snapshot plus three focused Rust probes: 85 passed.
- Six native guard mutations fail: re-publish, retry, finite cap, retry abort,
  supersession check and publication serialization.
- Seven Rust guard mutations fail: busy exemption, harness scope, native flag,
  interval floor, FYI busy bypass, persist-after-handoff ordering and event
  retirement. The final mutation actually ran both restart probes and failed
  both; a prior zero-test invocation was discarded, not counted as a pass.
- Two additional native race probes fail on the exact head and pass with the
  repair controls. Receipts: pr284-confirmed-races.log, pr284-native-mutations.json,
  pr284-rust-mutations.json, pr284-settlement-mutations.json.
- harness checks: exit 1, completed November 20, 2026 at 19:04:28 (+10), before
  the reported 19:23 process kill. Six stages passed, including the full Rust
  fmt/clippy/workspace-test gate, route inventory, smoke, native contracts,
  SDK contracts and skill structure. Eight dependency/tooling stages failed in
  this C25 worktree (missing local TS tools; incompatible ambient Biome).
  Attribution was an advisory warning. No local ship-readiness claim is made.

Static cost: one new bounded retry loop and timer, not a new poller or process
launch. Batch cutting uses the existing background tick; native Copilot delivery
is at most one batch per job per min_interval, and totals scale with jobs owned.
No live extension reload, daemon deployment or async-shell canary was performed.

Harness feedback: magicWand = make these registration-order, supersession and
restart-floor probes permanent contracts. Difficulties = C25's expected absent TS
dependencies, shared-build waiting, and the need for exact mutation selectors.
The private mutation driver now rejects zero-test runs and invokes shared-build
from the actual source root, which its under-lock freshness step requires.
The reviewed tracked worktree is unchanged; no dependency tree was installed.
Reviewer/284 holding is retained until merge.
